Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

unfortunately adverb

also sadly, unluckily, regrettably, I’m afraid (that), as bad luck would have it

classical

Cic. Att. 1.17.2: sed accidit perincommodē quod eum nusquam vīdistī
Caes. B.G. 5.33.4: tamen incommodē accidit

accidit incommodē (quod …)

phrase: accidit with the adverb, and a quod-clause for what happened

unfortunately (it so happened that)

Latin says that a thing turned out badly where English comments on it with an adverb. Perincommodē is “very unfortunately”. Incommodē alone is “inconveniently, at a bad moment” (Lewis & Short), and nōn incommodē is “quite conveniently”.

Other words

  • īnfēlīciter — unluckily, disastrously

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 328b: Immō enimvērō īnfēlīciter; Liv. 1.45.3 (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    Stronger than incommodē: of what ends in misfortune, a plan tried and failed.

  • nōllem — I wish it weren’t so; I’m sorry (that)

    imperfect subjunctive of nōlō, with an accusative or a perfect participle · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 165: Nōllem factum; Cic. Off. 1.35 (Lewis & Short): Carthāginem et Numantiam funditus sustulērunt; nōllem Corinthum · Wiktionary

    The speaker’s regret as a wish: nōllem factum, “I wish it hadn’t happened”, Terence’s stock apology. For a sigh of grief, heu (see alas).

Examples

  • sed accidit perincommodē quod eum nusquam vīdistī.

    But unfortunately you never saw him anywhere.Cic. Att. 1.17.2

  • Incommodē hercle. — Immō enimvērō īnfēlīciter.

    That’s bad luck. — No, it’s a disaster.Ter. Eun. 328–328b

  • Nōvī ego vestra haec: «Nōllem factum»; jūsjūrandum dabitur tē esse indignum injūriā hāc

    I know your sort: “I’m sorry it happened”; you’ll swear you never deserved such treatmentTer. Ad. 165–166

See also alas!, chance, I’m sorry, good luck!.
